p.src: A crystal has an additional kind of translation symmetry. Moving the whole crystal through space is an ordinary translation. For an infinite crystal, however, translation by one lattice spacing also returns the same physical arrangement. Equivalently, the lattice sites can be relabeled by shifting every site index by one. Boundaries spoil this exact statement for a finite crystal, but it becomes a good symmetry far from the ends of a very long crystal.

ja: 結晶にはさらに別種の並進対称性がある。結晶全体を空間中で動かすのは通常の並進である。しかし無限結晶に対しては、一格子間隔だけ並進させても同じ物理的配置が得られる。等価的に、すべての格子点の指数を1だけずらすことによって格子点を付け替えることができる。境界は有限結晶に対してこの厳密な主張を損なうが、非常に長い結晶の端から遠く離れたところでは良い対称性となる。
zh: 晶体还有一种额外的平移对称性。把整个晶体在空间中移动是普通的平移。然而，对于无限晶体，平移一个晶格间距也会得到相同的物理排列。等价地，可以通过把每个格点指标移动一来重新标记格点。对于有限晶体，边界会破坏这一精确陈述，但在很长的晶体中远离两端处，它成为一个良好的对称性。

zh: 空间的均匀性—即每个位置都与其他任何位置相同—就是平移对称性。空间的各向同性—即每个方向都与其他任何方向相同—就是旋转对称性。

p.src: Degeneracy is related to symmetry, but it is not the same thing. An energy level is degenerate when more than one state has exactly that energy. For a generic Hamiltonian with a discrete spectrum, an exact equality between two unrelated levels would be a remarkable accident. Agreement to one part in $10^{15}$ is still not exact equality. Exact degeneracies ordinarily point to symmetry.

p.src:
First consider a particle moving in the $xy$-plane, without restricting it to a circle. Under a small counterclockwise rotation, $\delta x=-\epsilon y,
\qquad
\delta y=\epsilon x.$ For the actively rotated state, the transformed wavefunction is evaluated at the inverse-rotated coordinates: $\psi_\epsilon(x,y)
=\psi(x+\epsilon y,y-\epsilon x).$ Consequently, $\begin{aligned}\delta\psi
&=\epsilon\left(
y\frac{\partial}{\partial x}
-x\frac{\partial}{\partial y}
\right)\psi
+\mathcal O(\epsilon^2)\\
&=-\frac{i\epsilon}{\hbar}
\left(xp_y-yp_x\right)\psi
+\mathcal O(\epsilon^2).\end{aligned}$ The generator of rotations about the $z$-axis is therefore $L_z=xp_y-yp_x.$ This is the $z$-component of the familiar classical vector $\mathbf L=\mathbf r\times\mathbf p.$ It is not only the mechanical angular momentum; in quantum mechanics it is the operator that generates rotations of the wavefunction. (The active-rotation convention is chosen to agree with the earlier transformation $\psi(\theta)\mapsto\psi(\theta-\epsilon)$ and with the final identification $L_z=xp_y-yp_x$ after the intermediate sign uncertainty in the spoken derivation.)
